source.author: verg
source.text: Quid loquar aut Scyllam Nisi, quam fama secuta est candida succinctam latrantibus inguina monstris Dulichias vexasse rates, et gurgite in alto, ah, timidos nautas canibus lacerasse marinis, aut ut mutatos Terei narraverit artus; quas illi Philomela dapes, quae dona pararit, quo cursu deserta petiverit, et quibus ante infelix sua tecta supervolitaverit alis?
source.text_original: Quid loquar aut Scyllam Nisi, quam fama secuta est / candida succinctam latrantibus inguina monstris / Dulichias vexasse rates, et gurgite in alto, / ah, timidos nautas canibus lacerasse marinis, / aut ut mutatos Terei narraverit artus; / quas illi Philomela dapes, quae dona pararit, / quo cursu deserta petiverit, et quibus ante / infelix sua tecta supervolitaverit alis?
source.text_english: Why should I speak of Scylla of Nisi, whom fame followed, bright, with barking monsters girdling her waist, to have harried the Dulichian ships, and, ah, in the deep surge to have torn frightened sailors with sea-dogs; or of how she may tell of Tereus’s changed limbs? What feast, what gifts Philomela prepared for him, by what course she sought the deserted place, and with what wings the unhappy woman had first flown above her own house?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: hanc feram et Charybdim Scyllamque succinctam multis canibus fugiens barbaros matrona sustinuit, quae nec naufragiis parceret nec captiuitatibus flecteretur.
reuse.text_original: hanc feram et Charybdim Scyllamque succinctam multis canibus fugiens barbaros matrona sustinuit, quae nec naufragiis parceret nec captiuitatibus flecteretur.
reuse.text_english: A barbarian matron, fleeing this wild beast and this Charybdis and Scylla girt with many dogs, endured it; she who would spare neither shipwrecks nor be bent by captivities.
